name: Claimlane
evidence: Headline: Claimlane bags €5.6M to turn product claims into business value

Summary: Aftersales product resolution platform Claimlane has raised €5.6million in a Series A funding round led by Verb Ventures, with participationfrom Skagerak Capital and Vendep Capital. The investment wil...

assessment.whatTheyDo: Claimlane is a Copenhagen-based B2B SaaS platform that helps retailers and brands manage returns, warranty and aftersales claims, and it has recently added an AI agent feature.
concerns: Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, so it is materially harder to join from the US. The only US signal is a third-party profile saying it is scaling in the US, and I could not confirm any US office or hiring.
I found no named founders, so founder technical depth is unverified.
I found no engineering roles. The only careers-related material was a generic third-party profile.
The product looks like vertical workflow SaaS for ecommerce returns and claims. I found no evidence of proprietary technology or data. The AI agent feature may be a thin layer on top.
The press headline says the Series A was €5.6M (about $5.6M). Search could not independently confirm it or Verb Ventures' lead. A May 2024 seed round of about €1.8M led by Vendep was confirmed.
A third-party profile lists 100-500 employees, which is larger than the small team this person wants. The figure is unverified and may be stale.
assessment.rationale: Claimlane is a real operating B2B SaaS company with a seed round and a Series A. It is in a mid-weight theme for this person, and I found no sign of deep technology. The Danish base, unknown founders, no engineering roles found and a possibly larger team all lower the score, but the company is real, so this is not a mismatch.
assessment.summary: Claimlane is a Copenhagen-based SaaS company that digitises returns, warranty and claims management for retail brands. It raised a €1.8M seed from Vendep Capital in 2024, and press reports a €5.6M Series A led by Verb Ventures in November 2026. It is a real product, but the fit for a US-based engineer is limited. The company is non-US, the founders and technical depth are unknown, and I found no engineering roles.
assessment.product: B2B SaaS that lets retail brands and retailers manage returns, warranty and aftersales claims workflows, with a newly launched AI agent feature.
assessment.team: Founders and leadership not identified in my searches. A third-party profile lists 100-500 employees, which is unverified.
assessment.funding: Seed of about €1.8M announced by Vendep Capital (reported May 2024). Press reports a €5.6M Series A in November 2026 led by Verb Ventures, with Skagerak Capital and Vendep Capital participating. Other seed investors listed on aggregator sites include Nicolaj Reffstrup and The Market Development Fund.
redFlags: Non-US headquarters
Founders unidentified
No engineering roles found
No evidence of proprietary technology
Reported headcount may be larger than the small team the person wants, and is unverified
Series A lead could not be independently confirmed
greenFlags: Real, shipping B2B SaaS product with paying retail customers implied
Institutional backing from Vendep Capital and, per press, Verb Ventures and Skagerak Capital
Round size is within the preferred range
Appears to be expanding into the US, which may mean US hiring

name: Harbinger
evidence: Headline: Harbinger raises $240M after expanding into defense
Summary: The Los Angeles-based startup has now raised more than $650 million, and is working on electric trucks, emergency vehicles, and a driverless platform for the military.

assessment.whatTheyDo: Harbinger Motors builds electric medium-duty commercial truck chassis (Class 4–7) with in-house software and controls, and has recently expanded into defense, including unmanned ground vehicles.
concerns: Defense expansion (In-Q-Tel and American Rheinmetall partnerships, a driverless military platform) is on the user's not-interested list.
This is automotive and EV hardware. It does not fit the user's software, AI, infrastructure or consumer interests, apart from the embedded and robotics theme.

The company is large and late-stage: the total raised is roughly $358M to $650M, and a $240M round is far above the preferred $2M to $150M range. An engineer would have less leverage than at a small team.
I could not find the $240M round in search results. They showed a $160M Series C co-led by FedEx, and reported totals vary by source.
Most engineering roles are embedded, firmware or automotive, which is a different stack from the user's cloud and web background.
assessment.rationale: Harbinger is a real, well-funded operating company with a founder from Anduril's hardware side and a shipped EV chassis product. But it is an automotive hardware and defense company, with a round far above the preferred size and a theme the user said they don't want. Only the embedded/robotics interest, which is weighted at 0.5, matches.
assessment.summary: Harbinger Motors is a Southern California EV commercial-chassis maker. It is led by John Harris, a former Anduril principal mechanical engineer, and it is backed by FedEx and THOR among others. It has moved into defense with unmanned ground vehicle work. It is a real product company, but it is capital-intensive hardware and defense-oriented, and it is large for an early-stage joining decision.
assessment.product: Electric medium-duty truck chassis, plus emergency vehicles and a driverless ground-vehicle platform for defense. Customers are fleet operators, with FedEx as an investor.
assessment.team: CEO and co-founder John Harris was previously a principal mechanical engineer at Anduril, where he led Sentry Tower hardware, and he also worked at Boeing, Faraday Future and Xos Trucks. I did not verify the other founders.
assessment.funding: A $100M Series B and a $160M Series C co-led by FedEx, with Technology Impact Fund (Capricorn) and THOR Industries returning. Press reports a new $240M round on 2026-11-05, which I did not independently confirm. Reported totals range from about $358M to over $650M.
redFlags: Defense pivot conflicts with the user's stated preferences.
Round sizes are far above the preferred range, and the company is capital-intensive.
The funding total is inconsistent across sources.
Vehicle hardware companies have a history of failing, and the founders are described as veterans of failed EV companies (Faraday, Xos).
greenFlags: A shipped product with a major customer relationship (FedEx).
The CEO has hardware depth from Anduril.
It is hiring senior software roles, including a VP of Software and managers.
A software, ADAS and data engineering team exists in-house.

name: MucoLife Therapeutics
evidence: Headline: MucoLife Therapeutics secures €91K from Vinnova to scale manufacturing of COPD treatment

Summary: MucoLife Therapeutics has received €91,000 (SEK 1 million) from Vinnova, Sweden’s innovation agency, through the call “Support to small and medium-sized companies for the use of life science infrastru...

assessment.whatTheyDo: Swedish preclinical biotech developing MLT-001, an inhaled drug that dissolves mucus plugs in COPD and cystic fibrosis.
concerns: Drug-development biotech, not software or tech, so it matches none of the person's interest themes
Headquartered in Sweden, which makes joining harder for a US-based person
The funding found is a SEK 1M (about €91K) grant, far below the $2M minimum round size
Preclinical, with Phase I trials expected between late 2026 and 2027 (sources disagree)
Roles would be in science and clinical work, not software engineering or product
assessment.rationale: MucoLife is a university spin-out pursuing an inhaled COPD drug. It has no software, AI or product-engineering angle, it is outside the US, and its funding is tiny grants. It is a clear mismatch for an engineer/PM looking at tech startups.
assessment.summary: MucoLife Therapeutics is a Gothenburg, Sweden biotech spun out of the University of Gothenburg's Mucin Biology Group. It is developing MLT-001, an inhaled mucus-dissolving therapy for COPD and cystic fibrosis. It has received small Vinnova grants and an investment from GU Ventures, and it joined the Health Wildcatters accelerator. It is a real company but not relevant to this person's interests.
assessment.product: MLT-001, a first-in-class inhaled therapy for dissolving pathological mucus plugs in COPD, cystic fibrosis and severe respiratory distress. A nebuliser device is also being planned.
assessment.team: Founded by Thaher Pelaseyed and Gunnar C. Hansson, from the University of Gothenburg's Mucin Biology Group (academic mucin biology researchers). I did not find other team details.
assessment.funding: Vinnova grant of SEK 1M (about €91K) reported in November 2026, an earlier Vinnova grant of SEK 300K (2025), a Medtech4Health/Vinnova grant for nebuliser planning, and an investment announced in 2024 by GU Ventures. The amount of that investment was not found.
redFlags: Preclinical biotech with no shipped product
Grant-funded and very small
Non-US headquarters
greenFlags: Founders have deep academic expertise in mucin biology
Accepted into the Health Wildcatters accelerator, selected from nearly 700 applicants

name: Onodrim
evidence: Headline: Onodrim raises $300m as European defence rollups heat up

assessment.whatTheyDo: European defence and industrial manufacturing roll-up that acquires and scales component and critical-system suppliers (radios, cameras, sensors) for military equipment.
concerns: It is a defence company, which is an explicit anti-interest.
The business model is acquiring manufacturers, not building software, so there is little engineering leverage of the kind this person wants.
It is headquartered in Europe, which makes it materially harder for a US-based person to join (visa, relocation or a time-zone gap).
I could not verify the $300M figure. Search results showed a €40M seed in Feb 2026 and a secondary source (Sacra) mentioning talks for about €200M. Treat the round size as unconfirmed.
A large raise with an early-stage, acquisition-led plan runs against their wariness of very large rounds without a shipped product.
assessment.rationale: Onodrim is a defence manufacturing roll-up based in Europe. That hits an explicit anti-theme and offers little software product work, and the geography adds a penalty. Only the round size and the Palantir-alumni founders are mildly positive.
assessment.summary: Onodrim (Onodrim Industries) is a European defence-tech platform founded by Palantir alumni and backed by Founders Fund, Lakestar and General Catalyst. It raised a €40M seed in Feb 2026 and is reported to be raising much more. It strategically buys and consolidates defence component suppliers. It is a poor fit for someone avoiding defence who wants a software product role in the US.
assessment.product: A platform that acquires and scales European defence and industrial component suppliers, for example radios, cameras and sensors, and sells to defence customers.
assessment.team: Described in press as founded by Palantir alumni (Bloomberg) and as Lithuanian-led (LRT, Intellinews). I did not verify individual founder names or backgrounds.
assessment.funding: €40M seed in Feb 2026, led by Founders Fund, Lakestar and General Catalyst. A Sifted headline reports $300M in Nov 2026, which I could not verify directly. Sacra mentions talks for about €200M in Sept 2026.
redFlags: Defence focus is an explicit anti-interest.
Roll-up model, not a software product company.
Based outside the US.
The $300M round size could not be independently verified.
greenFlags: Founders reportedly come from Palantir.
Backed by well-known investors (Founders Fund, General Catalyst, Lakestar).
Well funded.

name: Trajectory
evidence: Headline: Trajectory raises $45M to make AI model training accessible to nontechnical experts
Summary: The one-year-old startup is now valued at $300 million.

assessment.whatTheyDo: Trajectory builds a post-training and continual-learning platform that lets companies fine-tune open-source models on production feedback, with domain experts such as lawyers and doctors able to guide the process without deep technical skills.
matchedInterests: Agent frameworks, evaluation, and LLM tooling
Applied AI in a specific vertical (legal, health, finance, logistics)
concerns: The funding figures conflict across sources: TechCrunch says $45M Series A, others say $40M, and one aggregator mentions a $75M Series B. The $300M valuation on a one-year-old company is rich.
Crowded and well-funded competition (Thinking Machines' Tinker, Applied Compute, Prime Intellect) and the possibility that labs or customers build this in-house.
The 'accessible to nontechnical experts' pitch could shift engineering work toward UI/workflow rather than core research.
I could not confirm their own careers page. Open roles come from aggregators, and most are Member of Technical Staff research or generalist roles, with no confirmed senior/staff engineering openings.
Customer names come from press and are not independently verified.
assessment.rationale: The company is a real, shipping product in LLM tooling and post-training infrastructure with notable customers (Harvey, Rogo, Decagon, Mercor, Nvidia), and its founders have DeepMind and Apple research backgrounds. The team is about 18 people, so an engineer would have high leverage. Points are held back for crowded competition, valuation and funding ambiguity, and unverified senior engineering hiring.
assessment.summary: Trajectory is a roughly one-year-old San Francisco startup, founded by three Stanford classmates with DeepMind and Apple research backgrounds. It sells a platform for continually fine-tuning open-source models on real production feedback. It raised a Sequoia-led Series A at a $300M valuation, with Nvidia, Bessemer and Bain Capital Ventures participating. It looks like a strong technical place to work, with execution risk in a crowded space.
assessment.product: A post-training platform that connects open-source models to a customer's applications, collects feedback signals (edits, corrections, retries, rejections), and retrains the models continually. Domain experts can steer it without ML expertise. It is now publicly available, and customers are AI-native companies.
assessment.team: Co-founders Ronak Malde (CEO; ex-Google DeepMind, one of the researchers DeepMind acqui-hired from Windsurf), Michael Elabd (ex-Google DeepMind) and Arjun Karanam (ex-Apple, generative foundation models). About 18 people, with researchers and designers recruited from OpenAI, Stripe and Netflix.
assessment.funding: TechCrunch reports a $45M Series A led by Sequoia at a $300M valuation, with Nvidia, Bessemer Venture Partners and Bain Capital Ventures participating. Other outlets report $40M, and an earlier $15M round in May 2026. One aggregator mentions a $75M Series B, which I could not confirm.
openRoles: Member of Technical Staff - Design Eng
redFlags: Conflicting funding figures across sources
High valuation for a one-year-old company
Platform risk from labs and competitors with larger funding
No confirmed senior/staff engineer roles
greenFlags: Technical founders from DeepMind and Apple research
Shipping product with notable customers (Harvey, Rogo, Decagon, Mercor, Nvidia)
Team of about 18, so engineers are close to product decisions
Sequoia-led round with Nvidia participating
Based in San Francisco, a preferred location

name: Vensum Power
evidence: Headline: Vensum Power raises €9M to cut power losses in AI data centres, EV charging and energy storage

Summary: Finnish deeptech companyVensum Power has raised €9 million in a Series A funding round co-led byLifeline Ventures, Larsen & Toubro Group and Eviny Ventures. The investmentwill support the mass pro...

assessment.whatTheyDo: Finnish deeptech company building software-defined power converters (power electronics hardware plus firmware and cloud/IoT software) to cut power losses in AI data centres, EV charging and energy storage.
concerns: Headquartered in Espoo, Finland. The company is outside the US and no US hiring or remote option was found, so it is materially harder to join.
Core product is power-electronics hardware, which is only a loose match for the person's software, AI and infrastructure interests.
Only a small software component (IoT/cloud platform) was found, so most roles are likely hardware or power engineering.
No official careers page or company site was found, so roles and team size come from aggregators and may be stale.
The €9M Series A is known only from the tech.eu headline. I found no independent confirmation or detail in the searches.
assessment.rationale: This is a real, technical deeptech company with Lifeline Ventures behind it and a small team, but its focus is power electronics, which fits only the lowest-weight hardware theme. It is also based in Finland, which lowers the score. The fit is weak but not a clear mismatch.
assessment.summary: Vensum Power Oy is an Espoo-based Aalto spin-out founded around 2019 that builds software-defined power conversion technology. It raised a €3.8M seed in May 2023, led by Lifeline Ventures, and a €9M Series A reported in November 2026, co-led by Lifeline Ventures, Larsen & Toubro Group and Eviny Ventures. It is a credible hardware company, but it is a poor match for this person's software focus and US location.
assessment.product: Software-defined power converters for AI data centres, EV charging and energy storage, with cloud/edge IoT software for monitoring and control.
assessment.team: CEO Peter Nisula; Tero Lehtonen is listed as COO. Founder backgrounds were not found. Headcount is roughly 10 per one aggregator, which is possibly outdated.
assessment.funding: Seed of about €3.8M in May 2023, which included an R&D loan and a Business Finland grant. Investors were Lifeline Ventures (lead), Grid.vc and Harjavalta. A €9M Series A was reported on 2026-11-06, co-led by Lifeline Ventures, Larsen & Toubro Group and Eviny Ventures.
redFlags: Non-US headquarters with no sign of US hiring
Hardware-centric business
Open roles are listed only on aggregators, not on an official careers page
greenFlags: Real product and a deeptech moat
Small team, so an engineer would have leverage
Series A co-led by Lifeline Ventures, which also led the seed
Hiring a lead-level IoT/cloud developer
